title: Writing it down
hookLine: write what you've learned for those after you
tomorrow: a nine-year-old says thank you. who should Amira thank?

cards: A grandmother on speakerphone, telling the story of her own mother's prayer beads, the third time this year. Somebody says, I'll remember this one. Nobody quite does.
A phone can hold years of photos and not one minute of how she tells it. So how do you keep what an elder knows? The Qur'an names the tool right in its text: the pen.

teach.b: In Pickthall's words, God is the one "Who teacheth by the pen, Teacheth man that which he knew not." Another surah opens with an oath on the pen itself: "Nun. By the pen and that which they write (therein)."

And when the Qur'an turns to lending money, it starts with paperwork: "O ye who believe! When ye contract a debt for a fixed term, record it in writing." Writing protects people from their own memory.

A report in Sunan Abu Dawud tells of 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who wrote down what he heard the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say. Some people warned him off: he's human, they said, he speaks when he's angry and when he's pleased.
The Prophet pointed to his own mouth and told him to write, because nothing came from it but truth. Now the senses. Writing by hand is slow on purpose.
The scratch of the pen. The drag of ink. The weight of a page your hand had to fill.
A hand that's writing can't skim, so it keeps what a quick glance would lose. And a page, unlike a memory, can be handed to someone younger.
One to tell a friend tonight: the Qur'an swears an oath by the pen and that which they write.

how: Students of Islamic learning keep notebooks of what their teachers say, and some families write down a grandparent's duas, recipes and stories to pass on.

o: memorizing a lesson so well you never need notes
copying the Qur'an by hand as a work of calligraphy
keeping what you've learned on paper for those after you

games.q: what the pen keeps — tap the pairs.
p: told to write: nothing but truth

s: the Qur'an never mentions writing; it was only recited
it swears by the pen (68:1), names God as teaching by the pen (96:4), and asks that debts be written (2:282).
a report says the Prophet told 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr to keep writing
in Sunan Abu Dawud he pointed to his mouth: write, nothing comes from it but truth.
writing things down shows you don't trust your memory, so it's a weakness
2:282 asks for writing precisely so memory isn't the only witness.

games.q: your study group has one member who 'just remembers' everything and won't add to the shared notes. the exam is in a week, and she's sick for two days. what fits today?
o: trust her memory. she always knows it, so notes are busywork.
write the notes down together now, so nobody depends on one head.
wait until she's back. she'll fill everyone in afterward.
games.why: 2:282 asks for writing so no one relies on memory alone. a page can be handed on; a head can get sick.

practice: Take a pen and any scrap of paper. Write one thing someone older taught you, in their words if you can, with their name underneath. Go slowly enough to hear the pen move, and keep the page.

wordCard.voice: Writing it down: keeping what you've learned on paper for whoever comes after you. The Qur'an swears by the pen.

carryVoice: Pocket this: write it down, because a page waits when memory won't. Eight of ten, in ink.
